blocked: Found the right source but could not finish reading it. kensushiworkshop.org (the only web menu) is now confirmed unreliable, not just incomplete: its Special Tapas prices are stale against a dated (March 2026) in-store menu photo found on the restaurant's Google Maps listing - Salmon Crudo $25 vs real $27, Triple Belly Sampler $35 vs real $45, Kurobuta Sausage $9 vs real $10, Crispy Rice $18 vs real $21, Chilean Sea Bass Misoyaki $16 vs real $25, Ankimo $10 vs real $18 - and its Sake section bears no resemblance in names, count, or prices to the real one (real menu has ~20 sake items, .org has ~13, no overlap). The earlier finding that DoorDash's Entrees matched the .org at a clean 1.20x does not extend to other sections; the .org should not be used at all going forward. The real source is a set of physical-menu-page photos posted by a Google reviewer (Derrick Dupre) in March 2026, under the listing's Menu photo tab - confirmed legible pages for Sake and Starters/Special Tapas, both showing the restaurant's own logo. Could not page through to the Sashimi and Sushi & Rolls photos in the same set: the Google Maps photo carousel is virtualized (only ~3 thumbnails render in the DOM at a time) and repeatedly lost state or rendered black under heavy Chrome contention from sibling agents sharing the browser. This is a technical/session obstacle, not a missing menu - a future agent with a clear Chrome session should be able to page through the same photo set to the Sashimi/Sushi & Rolls pages.
